title: RBAC v2 migration: dual-write & backfill strategy with validation, audit logging, and customer communications
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Plan and execute migration from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 across Redwood platform. This ticket covers dual-write implementation, asynchronous backfill of historical grants, validation strategy for permissions parity, audit-log compatibility adjustments, SSO/SAML mapping checks, and the runbook + customer communication plan for cutover.
background: RBAC v2 introduces hierarchical role inheritance, scoped resource grants, and improved admin controls. Existing customers and services are on RBAC v1. We need a low-risk migration path that preserves current behavior, maintains audit trail continuity, and enables safe cutover without extended downtime.
approach: Phased migration: 1) Dual-write layer so writes populate both v1 and v2 schemas, 2) Backfill historical grants into v2 while monitoring parity, 3) Run comprehensive validation and access audits, 4) Execute staged cutover (controlled toggle per org), 5) Decommission v1 after confidence window. Maintain audit logging compatibility and confirm SSO/SAML role mappings map to v2 constructs.
migration_steps: Implement dual-write abstraction in auth service: feature-flagged, idempotent writes to v2 while preserving v1 writes
Add write-side schema version tagging and write-audit events for dual-write ops
Build backfill worker that iterates org-by-org and migrates grants, groups, and role bindings into v2 semantics
Create validation job that compares effective permission matrices between v1 and v2 for random samples and high-risk orgs
Update audit logging pipeline to include v2 grant change events and maintain field compatibility for downstream SIEMs
Coordinate SSO/SAML mapping update: map SAML attributes to v2 role constructs and test with test tenants
Expose an admin toggle at org-level for enabling RBAC v2 and a safety 'force-fallback' endpoint
Staged cutover: enable v2 for internal test orgs -> early adopter customers -> broad rollout with canary monitoring
Post-cutover: monitor for 7 days at P0/95th and P99 latency + permission error spikes before deprecating v1 reads/writes
validation_checks: Permission parity check: run nightly diff on a sample of 2k principals per org comparing allow/deny outcomes
End-to-end API smoke tests for admin actions, token issuance, SSO login flows, and service-to-service calls
Audit log integrity: ensure every v2 grant mutation emits legacy-compatible event fields for 30-day window
SSO/SAML mapping verification: synthetic login for top 10 enterprise customers and confirm roles assigned
Canary user simulation: simulate 1000 concurrent auth checks for real workloads against v2 to detect regression
monitoring_signals: Increase in 403/401 errors per org (alert threshold: +50% over baseline)
Backfill worker error rate and lag metrics (alert if >5% failures for 1h)
Dual-write divergence metric: percentage of writes where v1 != v2 acknowledgement
Audit log ingestion errors (Alert: any malformed v2 event to SIEM)
SLO: auth-check latency P95 must not regress more than 20ms vs baseline
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Permission mismatch causing customer outages. Mitigation: keep dual-read mode available and phased org toggles; emergency fallback to v1 reads
Risk: Backfill causes DB load. Mitigation: rate-limited backfill with per-org concurrency caps and traffic-aware windows
Risk: Audit log schema changes break downstream consumers. Mitigation: publish compatibility shim, iterate with Security & Integrations teams, and maintain legacy fields for 30 days
Risk: SSO attribute mapping differs across IdPs. Mitigation: create per-customer mapping overrides and test harness with SAML test certs
Risk: Complexity in dual-write leads to race conditions. Mitigation: write-idempotency via operation UUID and write-order checks
runbook: Pre-cutover checklist: all validation jobs green for 48h, backfill lag < 5%, dual-write divergence < 0.1%
Stage 1: flip feature flag for internal Redwood orgs; monitor 4h. If 403 spike >10% rollback immediately
Stage 2: invite early adopter customers (5 orgs) on weekend maintenance window; support on-call present
Stage 3: progressive ramp across orgs in batches of 50/day with automated gating based on monitoring_signals
Emergency rollback: set org toggle to v1-read for affected orgs and pause backfill workers; run hotfix to re-sync grants if needed
Post-cutover cleanup: schedule v1 read-only deprecation after 30 days and archive v1 schema snapshots
communication_plan: Internal: Security, Product, Support, Sales, and Solutions channels notified at start of cycle; daily standups during rollout
Customer: publish migration FAQ and timeline to https://docs.redwood.com/security/rbac-v2-migration; targeted emails to org admins 14/7/2 days before their toggle
Support playbook: triage steps, escalations, and canned responses for permission incidents; provide support runbook to SEs
Enterprise customers: schedule joint dry-run with SSO team and run through mapping report; offer opt-in early access
Public changelog: summary of v2 benefits, migration safeguards, and deprecation date for v1 (TBD post-confidence)

acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled behind flag and tested end-to-end
Backfill can migrate an org within SLA and exposes progress metrics
Validation jobs detect parity issues and alert with actionable diffs
SAML/SSO mappings verified for top 10 enterprise orgs
Audit logs emitted in backward-compatible format for the 30-day transition window
Support runbook published and on-call rotations allocated for rollout
notes: Decision: prefer dual-write + phased toggle to full live conversion to minimize blast radius
We maintain v1 for reads during the confidence window to avoid immediate customer-facing regressions
Backfill will be done incrementally starting with low-risk orgs (internal -> dev -> paid customers)
Consider adding a permissive simulation mode where v2 returns decision but not enforced to gather telemetry before toggles
